question: Was the small H12 uplift evidence for a specific and smooth momentum-diversification mechanism, or a local choice of horizon, split and weights?

required: moving-block familywise 90 percent lower uplift versus H12

variants.definition: Unrestricted ensemble leader plus best name in the opposite half of momentum-20; 50/50.
Replace momentum-20 with momentum-5; otherwise exact.
Replace momentum-20 with momentum-60; otherwise exact.
Momentum-20 half split with 75 percent leader and 25 percent opposite-half name.
Momentum-20 half split with 25 percent leader and 75 percent opposite-half name.
Leader plus best name in the farthest momentum-20 tercile; 50/50.
Leader plus best name on the opposite side of zero momentum-20 rank; median split fallback; 50/50.
Leader plus best opposite-half name only if it is in ensemble top 10; otherwise second ensemble name; 50/50.
Leader plus the ensemble-top-20 name maximizing ensemble mean minus 0.10 times absolute pair-average momentum-20 exposure; 50/50.
Best name from the bottom momentum-20 tercile plus best name from the top tercile; 50/50.
Cross-sectionally residualize ensemble mean against momentum-20 alone and take the top two; 50/50.

interpretation.specificity_support: The momentum-20 reference should beat at least four of five unrelated split variables and neither adjacent horizon should reverse its result.
interpretation.smoothness_support: At least two of the alternative weights/splits should remain above the original L4 control at net20 and after top-20 winning-day removal.
interpretation.promotion: No outcome can promote production; this round can only retain or falsify the mechanism for forward shadow.
